rules: Frame 0 is a satellite map already moving (zoom-in or pan), never a still or a title card; narration and the first caption start at 0.0-0.2 s, first pin or card by 1.5 s.
Open with a geographical paradox, stark dividing line (e.g. 80% vs 20% split), impossible barrier (Pan-American Highway gap), or counter-intuitive proximity (US-Russia 3.8 km).

Hard cuts only where the visual type changes (map to archival photo, B-roll clip, 3D globe, or diagram). Moving between places on one map stays inside one long map segment with a continuous camera path (zoom-out -> pan -> deep zoom-in up to 16x), never a cut between two segments of the same map.
At most 0.41 hard cuts per 10 s; first hard cut at 21 s or later.
The camera never holds still: continuous drift >= 0.06 ln/s between camera moves, no hold over 1.7 s (hard limit 3.0 s), with 3D pitch/tilt on terrain and close-up beats.
Something new on screen every 1-3 s: a pin, a region fill, a flag badge, a dashed distance line, an animated counter, a route segment, or a new shot.

Typography on dark satellite maps uses clean geometric sans-serif (Inter Bold / SemiBold): ALL CAPS for country and mountain range names, Title Case with white dot + straight leader line for cities, enclaves, islands, and straits.

Quantify geographical claims visually using high-contrast pill badges (yellow/cyan/red), animated number counters (days, km, population), dashed measurement lines with metric + imperial units, or familiar city polygon scale overlays (e.g. NYC over Andorra).

Distinguish territories clearly using translucent entity fills with glowing borders, diagonal striped fills for multi-country comparisons or blocked zones, full flag-map fills, or floating flag cards.
Captions stay at fixed y = 1190 (bottom <= 1250 px, Shorts safe zone), Inter SemiBold, 2 words per event, thin outline and soft drop shadow, no per-word highlight and no box.
Watermark 'Geoverum' stays clear at the watermark top right (32 px clearance).
Music and SFX come from Epidemic Sound only, mixed to -14.0 LUFS (-1.5 dBTP) with music ducked -12 dB under the voiceover and no silence gap over 0.65 s.
The last 5 s return to a keyword or title from the hook on screen (or a 3D globe macro summary); No call to action and no end card.

liked.what: continuous multi-stop camera path across one map instead of cutting between map shots
liked.why: preserves spatial orientation from macro continent scale down to 16x enclave/island close-ups

liked.what: year or hero percentage held big and clean before supporting pill badges appear
liked.why: one clear focal point per beat without competing text

liked.what: geographical paradox hook with an instant dividing line or blocked route in the first 1.5 s
liked.why: immediately hooks viewer curiosity with a visual contradiction (80/20 line, Darien Gap X, US-Russia 3.8 km)

liked.what: blackout political map with sequential 1..N neighbor counter
liked.why: isolates countries on dark charcoal land so each highlighted border pops unmistakably

liked.what: dashed distance callout line with metric and imperial units (e.g. 2 km / 1.24 mi, 85 m / 279 ft)
liked.why: makes border anomalies, enclaves, and strait widths immediately concrete

liked.what: city or landmark scale comparison overlay (e.g. NYC polygon overlaid on Andorra or interior West)
liked.why: translates abstract area or population figures into an instant visual reference

liked.what: flag-map polygon fill, diagonal striped territory hatch, and floating flag badges with leader lines
liked.why: identifies sovereign ownership at a glance during enclave and disputed-island close-ups

liked.what: 3D tilted terrain with animated rain clouds or freeze texture spreading across straits
liked.why: shows physical geography and climate mechanisms (rain shadow, seasonal ice bridge) instead of just naming them

rejected.what: hard cut between two segments of the same map
rejected.why: breaks spatial continuity; use a camera path on one map segment

rejected.what: static frame or camera hold over 1.7 s
rejected.why: violates P01/P02; the map or still must keep drifting

rejected.what: call to action or subscribe end card
rejected.why: Geoverum ends on the final factual twist or keyword return

rejected.what: unquantified geographic claims without a line, counter, pill badge, or pin on the map
rejected.why: every spoken distance, percentage, or border count must have a matching visual anchor on screen

rejected.what: cluttered multi-line paragraphs or backing boxes on captions
rejected.why: obscures the satellite map and violates Geoverum's clean lower-zone caption style
